newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Airways suffers first half loss.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Airways suffers first half loss.

text.p: Cyprus Airways reported a 2.9 million pound ($6.27 million) loss on Tuesday, blaming poor booking levels, a crisis in tourism and soaring costs from fuel price rises.

The accounts, approved by the airline's board on Monday, include a one-off cash grant of 2.6 million pounds from the government to Cyprus Airways this year. Without this abnormal item, the first half loss would have been 5.5 million pounds.
"We are expecting the second half to go better," airline spokesman Tassos Angeli told Reuters. "There is a general crisis in tourism and it was inevitable that Cyprus Airways would be affected."
Passenger figures, he said, were down by "several thousands".
Arrivals to the eastern Mediterranean island, which heavily depends on tourism, were 3.9 percent lower this summer season, according to official data.

The cash grant represents fees paid by Cyprus Airways to Eurocontrol, the air traffic control association of Europe, between 1991 and 1995. The Cypriot government, which receives a portion of Eurocontrol's proceeds, returned the sum to the airline on a one-off basis, the company said.

The government controls 80 percent of Cyprus Airways. The remaining 20 percent is traded on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE). On Monday Cyprus Airways share price fell to a year low of 40 cents from its close of 42 cents on Friday.
Losses were also reported to Cyprus Airways's subsidiary Eurocypria, a charter airline firm. But most of the losses were suffered by Cyprus Airways, Angeli said.
He said an increase in fuel costs by 0.4 million pounds and the firmness of the Cyprus pound against weaker currencies also had an impact.

Asked whether the airline will follow other companies and hike its fares in response to rising fuel prices, Angeli said: "At some stage we will have to look at this but we are up against strong competition from airlines reducing their fares all the time."
